reviewChoiceGroups.title: Architecture disposition
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how to handle platform-based mobile/desktop shell selection.

options.label: Single branch + platform detector
options.description: Render exactly one shell from App.tsx using a small isMobileBrowserPlatform detector.
options.rationale: Matches the user requirement while avoiding duplicate DOM, duplicate labels, and CSS breakpoint drift.

options.label: Responsive CSS selector
options.description: Use viewport breakpoints to choose mobile vs desktop shell.
options.rationale: Best general UX, but conflicts with the explicit platform-based requirement.

options.label: Layout service + user toggle
options.description: Add a layout service and persisted manual override now.
options.rationale: Useful later for iPad ambiguity, but overbuilt for the smallest safe version.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Code quality stance
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how much code structure this focused layout decision needs.

options.label: Pure detector + small hook
options.description: Keep isMobileBrowserPlatform pure and usePlatformLayout as a thin hook wrapper.
options.rationale: This is the easiest path to unit-test without creating a layout service.

options.label: Component tests only
options.description: Hide detector details inside React and test App rendering only.
options.rationale: Less exported API, but harder to cover UA edge cases cleanly.

options.label: Split shell files now
options.description: Extract MobileShell and DesktopShell files immediately.
options.rationale: Reasonable if App.tsx grows, but not necessary for this reduced scope.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Runtime validation requirement
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the minimum runtime UI test matrix before accepting the change.

options.label: Platform + viewport matrix
options.description: Test desktop-wide, desktop-narrow, mobile-phone, and mobile-wide shell selection; run full flow on one mobile and one desktop scenario.
options.rationale: This directly proves platform selection is not accidentally viewport selection while keeping runtime cost manageable.

options.label: Two flow tests only
options.description: Run one desktop and one mobile core flow without narrow/wide cross-checks.
options.rationale: Faster, but it will not catch viewport-based regression.

options.label: Unit-only detector tests
options.description: Rely on unit tests for platform detection and skip browser matrix changes.
options.rationale: Insufficient because the user specifically prefers runtime UI testing across scenarios.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Performance and risk response
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how to manage UA ambiguity and runtime artifact risk.

options.label: Document caveats + synthetic artifacts
options.description: Document UA/iPad caveats, keep platform detection layout-only, reset test storage, and use synthetic screenshots.
options.rationale: Accepts known UA imperfection without adding product complexity or privacy risk.

options.label: Add override now
options.description: Add a local setting to force mobile or desktop layout.
options.rationale: Reduces misclassification risk but introduces new UI, persistence, and test work.

options.label: Ignore caveats
options.description: Ship platform detection with no documented limitations or special tests.
options.rationale: Fastest, but brittle and likely to regress on iPad/tablet scenarios.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Final disposition
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the final implementation readiness decision for platform layout selection.

options.label: Approve reduced scope with test guardrails
options.description: Proceed with one detector and one rendered shell, after adding the runtime matrix guardrails.
options.rationale: The architecture is small enough; the main missing piece is valid platform-based runtime coverage.

options.label: Request runtime matrix first
options.description: Do not accept implementation until Playwright projects prove platform vs viewport behavior.
options.rationale: Choose this if test correctness is considered blocking before any further code review.

options.label: Reject platform detection
options.description: Redesign around responsive layout rather than browser platform.
options.rationale: Best general UX, but contradicts the selected product requirement.
